# `nish/net/outbound`

The policy for a program that fetches URLs it did not choose: a webhook sender, a link previewer, an importer that takes a URL from a form. Without one, such a program is a proxy into its own network for whoever supplies the URL (server-side request forgery): a URL naming `127.0.0.1`, `169.254.169.254` or a name that resolves to either reaches services that trust the program's address.

```ts
import {
  OutboundPolicy,
  outboundAddressAllowed,
  outboundAddressPublic,
  outboundAddressText,
  outboundFilter,
  outboundHostAllowed,
} from "nish/net/outbound";
```

```ts
import { OutboundPolicy } from "nish/net/outbound";
import { HttpOptions } from "nish/net/fetch";

const options = new HttpOptions();
options.outbound = new OutboundPolicy();
```

<scalar-detail title="The check is on the address, after the lookup">

A name is never judged
by its text: `nish/net/fetch` resolves it, drops every address
`outboundAddressAllowed` refuses, and connects only to the bytes it kept,
with no second lookup, so a name whose answer changes between a check and
a connect (DNS rebinding) cannot move the connection. Every redirect hop is
dialled the same way, so a public URL that redirects inward is refused at
the hop.

</scalar-detail>

<scalar-detail title="Public">

**Public** is the IANA special-purpose registries read strictly
(RFC 6890, and the registries at iana.org/assignments/iana-ipv4-special-registry
and iana-ipv6-special-registry). An IPv4 address is public unless it is in
`0/8`, `10/8`, `100.64/10`, `127/8`, `169.254/16`, `172.16/12`,
`192.0.0/24`, `192.0.2/24`, `192.88.99/24`, `192.168/16`, `198.18/15`,
`198.51.100/24`, `203.0.113/24`, `224/4` or `240/4` (the broadcast
address included), or is `168.63.129.16`, a cloud host's metadata and DNS
service. An IPv6 address is public only in `2000::/3`, and then not in
`2001::/23` (Teredo included), `2001:db8::/32` or `3fff::/20`; `2002::/16`
(6to4) and `64:ff9b::/96` (NAT64) are judged by the IPv4 address they carry,
as is `::ffff:0:0/96`, the form every IPv4 address takes in `nish:net`.
Everything else, `::1`, `fc00::/7` and `fe80::/10` among it, is refused.

</scalar-detail>

`permit` lets a trusted prefix through anyway (an internal API the program
is meant to reach), and `allowHost` narrows the names a URL may carry. The
policy also caps a fetch's redirects, total time and body, and the client
uses the stricter of these and its own options.

Private helpers share the importing program's flat symbol namespace
(`docs/wp26-stdlib.md` §3e), which is why each one carries the module's name.

Written from RFC 6890, RFC 4291, RFC 6052, RFC 3056, RFC 4380 and the IANA
special-purpose address registries, not ported from another implementation.

## outboundAddressAllowed

Whether `policy` lets a connection go to the sixteen address bytes at
`addr[off]`: a prefix it `permit`s, or else a public address.

```ts
function outboundAddressAllowed(
  policy: OutboundPolicy,
  addr: u8[],
  off: i32,
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="policy" type="OutboundPolicy" required>

The policy whose permits are checked first.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="addr" type="u8[]" required>

The array holding the address; an IPv4 one in its `::ffff:` form, as nish:net writes it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the address's sixteen bytes start in `addr`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when a connection may go there. An IPv4 address carried by NAT64 or 6to4 is judged as that address, by a permit too.

</scalar-field>

## outboundAddressPublic

Whether the sixteen address bytes at `addr[off]` are public, as the module
comment defines it. Panics when sixteen bytes do not fit there.

```ts
function outboundAddressPublic(
  addr: u8[],
  off: i32,
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="addr" type="u8[]" required>

The array holding the address; an IPv4 one in its `::ffff:` form, as nish:net writes it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the address's sixteen bytes start in `addr`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True for a public address. An IPv4 one carried by NAT64 or 6to4 is judged as that IPv4 address.

</scalar-field>

## outboundAddressText

The sixteen address bytes at `addr[off]` as text, for an error to name.

```ts
function outboundAddressText(
  addr: u8[],
  off: i32,
): string
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="addr" type="u8[]" required>

The array holding the address.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="off" type="i32" required>

Where the address's sixteen bytes start in `addr`.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="string">

Dotted decimal for an IPv4 address in its `::ffff:` form, otherwise all eight lower-case hex groups with no `::` shortening.

</scalar-field>

## outboundFilter

Keeps the addresses of `count` `DNS_ADDRESS_BYTES` records in `addresses`
that `policy` allows, moved to the front in their order, and answers how
many. Refused records are left behind them, so the caller can name one.

```ts
function outboundFilter(
  policy: OutboundPolicy,
  addresses: u8[],
  count: i32,
): i32
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="policy" type="OutboundPolicy" required>

The policy each address is checked against, as `outboundAddressAllowed` checks it.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="addresses" type="u8[]" required>

The records, each sixteen address bytes and a two-byte port, reordered in place.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="count" type="i32" required>

How many records `addresses` holds from its start; one that does not fit panics.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="i32">

How many records were kept, now `addresses`' first ones; 0 when every one was refused.

</scalar-field>

## outboundHostAllowed

Whether `policy` lets a URL name `host`, as the URL parser gives it
(lower-cased, an IPv6 literal without its brackets). Any host when the
policy names none.

```ts
function outboundHostAllowed(
  policy: OutboundPolicy,
  host: string,
): boolean
```

#### Parameters

<scalar-field name="policy" type="OutboundPolicy" required>

The policy whose `allowHost` names are checked.

</scalar-field>

<scalar-field name="host" type="string" required>

The URL's host; its case and one trailing dot do not matter.

</scalar-field>

#### Returns

<scalar-field name="returns" type="boolean">

True when the host is one the policy names, or under a `.`-led name it allows, or the policy names none.

</scalar-field>

## OutboundPolicy

What a client that fetches untrusted URLs may reach. A new policy refuses
every address that is not public, allows any host name, and caps a fetch
at 5 redirects, 30 seconds and an 8 MiB body.

```ts
class OutboundPolicy
```

| Member | |
| --- | --- |
| `new OutboundPolicy()` | Makes the default policy the class describes: public addresses only, any host name, and the default limits. |
| `maxBodyBytes: i64` | A fetch's body is cut off past this, or past the client's own cap if lower. |
| `maxRedirects: i32` | At most this many redirects, or the client's own limit if lower. |
| `permitted: u8[]` | `OUTBOUND_PERMIT_BYTES` per prefix `permit` let through. |
| `totalTimeoutMs: i32` | A whole fetch ends after this, or the client's own budget if lower; 0 or less for the client's alone. |
| `allowHost(name: string): void` | Adds `name` to the hosts a URL may name; once any is added, a URL (or a redirect) naming another is refused before it is looked up. Case and one trailing dot do not matter. A leading dot (`.example.com`) allows the name and every name under it. An address literal matches only itself, as the URL writes it (`::1` or `[::1]`, `127.0.0.1`), never as a suffix. |
| `permit(cidr: string): boolean` | Lets the addresses in `cidr` through though they are not public: `10.1.2.0/24`, `fd00:1::/64`, or one address alone. False, with nothing added, when `cidr` is not an address and a prefix length that fits it. |
